text: The Fernández Anchorena Palace is an architecturally significant former residence located in the Recoleta section of Buenos Aires, Argentina, and currently functions as the Apostolic Nunciature in Argentina. It was commissioned by Juan Antonio Fernández and his wife, Rosa de Anchorena, to the French Argentine architect Eduardo Le Monnier (1873–1931), who designed it in 1907 in the Second Empire style, which was popular among Argentine high society at the time. The palace was completed in 1909, although the Fernández-Archorena couple never lived there. Over the years, the family used the mansion for social events and public ceremonies, and from 1922 to 1928, it served as the official residence of President Marcelo Torcuato de Alvear and his wife, the opera chanteuse Regina Pacini de Alvear. In 1940, the property was sold to Adelia María Harilaos de Olmos, the widow of prominent Córdoba Province landowner Ambrosio Harilaos de Olmos. She was the founder of the Catholic Ladies' League and a financier of a working women's assistance fund, as well as a contributor to several churches and a hospital pavilion. In 1947, she bequeathed the residence to the Holy See. Following her death in 1949, the palace became the Apostolic Nunciature in Argentina. At the time, Pope Pius XII had previously been a guest of hers (as Cardinal Pacelli) during his visit to Buenos Aires in 1934 for the Eucharistic Congress. The palace's geographic coordinates are 34°35′22″S 58°23′09″W (34.58944°S 58.38583°W).
